text:
maya: Noticing multiple nodes in eu-west1 with exactly one GPU-heavy pod each, blocking batch queues. Pending backlog climbing.
jon: Same - looks like strict podAntiAffinity + nodeSelector:gpu=ampere. Leaves single-pod islands.
leo: Also many of those pods tolerate taint gpu=dedicated:NoSchedule and use local PVs for scratch. Tough to evict.
anuj: Can you paste events for one pending pod?
maya: kubectl describe pod batch-912 -n ml | grep -A3 Events
maya: Normal Scheduled 8m default-scheduler Assigned to node-gpu-eu-west1-b-11
maya: Warning FailedMount 7m kubelet MountVolume.SetUp failed for volume "scratch-local": node affinity mismatch
jon: That local PV is the blocker - preempting would break volume affinity so scheduler avoids it.
sam: Cost impact: AZ imbalance - some racks at 95% while others underutilized. We're spinning on-demand elsewhere; billing +6% week over week.
leo: Quick mitigation: run descheduler RemoveDuplicates and LowNodeUtilization targeting pods >24h old and excluding pods with annotation scratch-local=true.
anuj: Long-term fixes: (1) admission webhook to downgrade required anti-affinity to preferred for low-priority batch, (2) label a subset of nodes batch=true for consolidation, (3) offer remote-backed scratch volumes to reduce local PV stickiness.
maya: Ops request: can infra run a canary descheduler tonight at 23:00 UTC? I'll own rollback runbook.
jon: I'll run it and watch. Command: kubectl run descheduler-canary -n kube-system --image=descheduler:latest -- --policy-file=/etc/descheduler/policy-canary.yaml
sam: Add alerting: if PodPreemptionRate > 4/min or PendingBatchJobs > 150 for >10m then rollback. Also cost team will monitor reserved vs actual utilization.
leo: Note: NVLink contention when packing multiple heavy jobs has shown p95 regression in earlier tests. Run microbench after canary before wider rollout.
maya: Timeline: canary tonight, perf microbench tomorrow AM, decide next week. Thanks all.
